class_name: 授受-内の授与-テヤル類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Sends an action outward as a favor, from the speaker's side to someone who is neither owed honorifics nor talked down to (弟の弁当に卵焼きを入れてあげた). 〜てやる is the blunt downward member of the same ladder and 〜て差し上げる the humble one. Because it names the act as a favor, saying it to the beneficiary's face can sound self-congratulatory, so a plain form or お〜します is safer when actually offering.

examples.ruby: 弟[おとうと]のお弁当[べんとう]に卵焼[たまごや]きを入[い]れてあげた。
examples.english: I put some tamagoyaki in my little brother's lunchbox for him.

examples.ruby: 道[みち]に迷[まよ]っている人[ひと]を交番[こうばん]まで案内[あんない]してあげた。
examples.english: I walked a lost stranger over to the police box.

examples.ruby: 見[み]えにくいなら、私[わたし]の席[せき]と替[か]えてあげるよ。
examples.english: If you can't see well, I'll swap seats with you.

patterns.usage_note: The same outward favor as 〜てあげる, aimed downward at children, juniors, animals or plants (犬を散歩に連れてやる); directed at anyone else it reads as rude, and in speech it is typically male. With no beneficiary at all it voices defiant resolve in the volitional (絶対に勝ってやる, 見返してやる), the use that most often separates it from 〜てあげる in conversation.

examples.ruby: 落[お]ち込[こ]んでいる後輩[こうはい]に昼飯[ひるめし]をおごってやった。
examples.english: I bought lunch for a junior colleague who was down in the dumps.

examples.ruby: 今度[こんど]こそ結果[けっか]を出[だ]して見返[みかえ]してやる。
examples.english: This time I'll deliver, and I'll show them all.

examples.ruby: 猫[ねこ]が鳴[な]くので、窓[まど]を細[ほそ]く開[あ]けてやった。
examples.english: The cat kept meowing, so I cracked the window open for him.

glosses: do … for a superior or customer
patterns.usage_note: Does something for a superior, a guest or a customer, with 差し上げる lowering the doer (荷物を運んで差し上げる). 〜てあげる is the neutral member of the same ladder and 〜てやる the blunt downward one. It keeps あげる's favor-doing flavor, so addressed to the person's face it often lands as condescending; business-manner guides prefer お〜する (お荷物をお部屋までお運びします) when speaking to them directly.

examples.ruby: お客様[きゃくさま]の荷物[にもつ]を部屋[へや]まで運[はこ]んで差[さ]し上[あ]げてください。
examples.english: Please carry the guest's luggage up to their room.

examples.ruby: 会長[かいちょう]のためにお車[くるま]を手配[てはい]して差[さ]し上[あ]げました。
examples.english: I arranged a car for the chairman.

examples.ruby: 先生[せんせい]のご都合[つごう]を先方[せんぽう]に伝[つた]えて差[さ]し上[あ]げた。
examples.english: I passed the professor's availability along to the other party for him.
